mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the previous 6 months indicates a strong demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances where HOUST shows a sustained increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which is typically associated with stronger economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous 3 months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies adjust to reduced output and lower earnings.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO declines by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 5% over the previous 6 months signals strong consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances where RSAFS increases by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, the combination signals a tight monetary policy with a strong labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to increased borrowing costs and wage pressures.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy with strong labor market
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the previous month signals a strong labor market, which is typically associated with stronger economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% over the previous quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies adjust to reduced demand and lower earnings.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where GDPC1 declines by more than 1%.
